200 g lor: Peel the peppers and chop finely.
Mash the lor with a fork.
Add the garlic and oil.
Mix in the pepper.
Garnish with chilli flakes and parsley.
Lor is low in salt; taste and add salt as needed.
Cumin chickpea meze
Make a dressing with oil, lemon, cumin and salt.
Toss the chickpeas with the dressing.
Serve with parsley.
Letting it rest for a while lets the flavours settle.
Purslane yogurt meze
Pick the purslane leaves and wash them.
Chop coarsely.
Add the purslane.
Drizzle with olive oil.
Purslane is rich in omega-3.
Garlic broccoli meze
Boil the broccoli for 4 minutes and plunge into cold water.
Chop finely.
Whisk the yogurt, garlic and salt.
Add the broccoli.
Drizzle with oil sizzled with chilli flakes.
Overcooked broccoli gives off a sulphur smell.
Cauliflower tahini meze
Separate the cauliflower into florets and roast at 220 °C for 25 minutes.
Let cool and mash.
Whisk the tahini, lemon, garlic and cumin.
Mix with the cauliflower.
Serve with olive oil.
Roasting tastes better than boiling.
Chard yogurt meze
Finely chop the chard.
Wilt in oil and cook until the liquid evaporates.
Let cool.
Mix with the yogurt and garlic.
Chop the thick stems separately and cook them first.
Eggplant and tomato meze (roasted ezme)
Roast and peel the eggplant and peppers.
Peel the tomato and dice small.
Chop everything finely.
Mix with garlic, oil, pomegranate molasses and salt.
Roasting gives a smoky flavour.
Celeriac and apple meze
1 celeriac root
2 tablespoons mayonnaise (optional)
Grate the celeriac and apple; drizzle with lemon so they don’t brown.
Mix with the yogurt (and mayonnaise).
Add the walnuts.
Let rest for 30 minutes.
Lemon stops the celeriac from browning.
Cream-free vegetable soup
3 cups chopped vegetables (zucchini, carrot, broccoli, cauliflower, leek, celeriac or pumpkin)
5 cups hot water or vegetable stock
Fry the onion in olive oil and butter for 3 minutes.
Add the vegetables and diced potato and stir for 5 minutes.
Add the hot water and salt; once boiling, cook over low heat for 20–25 minutes until the vegetables are soft.
Blend until smooth, add the milk and simmer for 2 minutes.
Season with black pepper and serve hot.
Carrot–ginger, cauliflower–turmeric, pumpkin–cinnamon and zucchini–dill are good pairings.
Potato gives a velvety texture without cream.
Serve hot with crispy bread and lemon.
Roasted pepper and tomato soup
3 roasted kapia peppers
2 ripe tomatoes
Wash and trim the vegetables; cut the main ingredient into small, even pieces.
Fry the onion in olive oil for 3 minutes; add the roasted pepper and tomato (fresh herbs, lemon or yogurt are added when serving).
Add the water and cook over a gentle heat for 20–25 minutes until everything is completely soft.
Blend if needed; add fresh herbs and lemon juice after taking off the heat, and yogurt only after tempering it.
Chickpea and lemon soup
Fry the onion in olive oil for 3 minutes; add the chickpeas (fresh herbs, lemon or yogurt are added when serving).
Vegetable stew
3 cups chopped vegetables (zucchini, eggplant, leek, cauliflower, broccoli, spinach or celeriac)
1 cup cooked chickpeas or green lentils
Fry the onion in olive oil for 4 minutes and the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the tomato paste and stir until fragrant.
Add the firm vegetables (celeriac, cauliflower, leek) first and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the soft vegetables and the chickpeas or lentils, then the hot water and salt.
Cook covered over low heat for 20–25 minutes; let rest for 10 minutes.
Add the vegetables in order of cooking time so they all soften at once.
Serve hot with yogurt and rice pilaf.
Green salad with grains
1 cup cooked grains (bulgur, wheat, buckwheat or green lentils)
1 bunch rocket or purslane
2 tablespoons pomegranate molasses or lemon juice
Cook the grains al dente according to the packet and let cool.
Wash and dry the greens and chop coarsely.
Chop the cucumber and onion and halve the tomatoes.
Toss all the ingredients with the dressing and serve immediately.
Adding beetroot, pear, orange or walnuts turns the salad into a main meal.
Without the dressing it keeps for 1 day in the fridge.
Oven-baked vegetable frittata
6 eggs
4 tablespoons milk
1.5 cups chopped vegetables (zucchini, mushroom, potato, broccoli, tomato or spinach)
1 cup grated kashar or crumbled white cheese
4–5 sprigs dill or parsley
Melt the butter in an ovenproof pan and sauté the vegetables for 5–6 minutes.
Whisk the eggs with the milk, salt and pepper and add half the cheese.
Pour the mixture over the vegetables and cook on the hob for 2 minutes until the edges set.
Sprinkle with the remaining cheese and bake for 12–15 minutes until set in the middle.
Let rest for 5 minutes and slice.
If using potato, boil it for 5 minutes first.
Slice and serve hot or lukewarm.
Grain pilaf with vegetables
1.5 cups grains (bulgur, rice, quinoa, buckwheat or orzo)
1 cup diced vegetables (carrot, peas, eggplant, spinach or red pepper)
As much hot water as the grain needs (bulgur/rice: 2.5–3 cups, quinoa: 2.5 cups)
If using rice, soak in lukewarm water for 20 minutes and wash; rub the quinoa while washing.
Fry the onion in olive oil for 3 minutes, add the vegetables and sauté for 4 minutes.
Add the grains and toast for 2 minutes.
The water ratio depends on the grain; check the packet instructions.
Chicken sauté with plenty of vegetables
600 g chicken breast (diced)
2 cups chopped vegetables (zucchini, mushroom, carrot, broccoli, red pepper, peas or leek)
1 tablespoon tomato paste (optional)
1 dessert spoon thyme or rosemary
Cut the chicken on a separate chopping board and toss with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a wide pan and sear the chicken over high heat for 6–7 minutes until browned on all sides, then remove.
